title: Pizza with beans and vegetables, thin crust

content.title: About
content.content: A thin, crispy pizza topped with tomato sauce, quality beans, fresh vegetables (bell pepper, onion, zucchini, tomatoes) and a light layer of mozzarella cheese. A perfect choice for a light yet satisfying vegetarian snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beans boost the plant‑based protein and fiber content of the pizza.
Thin crust is baked without added oil, reducing calories compared with traditional pizza.
The vegetables used are rich in vitamins A, C, and K.
Tomato sauce provides lycopene, a powerful antioxidant.
Bean‑topped pizza is a common Mediterranean alternative to meat‑based pies.

items.title: Rich source of plant protein
items.content: Beans deliver about 7 g of protein per serving, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes lasting satiety.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Thin crust and modest cheese amount make this pizza more heart‑friendly.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Vegetables supply vitamin C, potassium, and folate, important for immunity and metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Tomato sauce and vegetables contain lycopene and carotenoids that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Tomato sauce and cheese can increase sodium levels; those monitoring blood pressure should choose a low‑salt version.

items.title: Gluten in crust
items.content: Thin crust is typically wheat‑based; people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should look for a gluten‑free alternative.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Reheat the pizza in a 180 °C oven for 5‑7 minutes until the crust is crisp. Optionally top with fresh arugula or basil after heating.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cooked pizza in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze in freezer‑safe bags for up to 1 month. Thaw in the fridge before reheating.
